scenes.heading: Simplifying algebraic fractions
scenes.say: Fractions with letters can look scary, but every one of them is simplified the same way. In this video you will learn to factorise first and then cancel.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Take the same whole block off both sides of a balance
scenes.science: Cancel the same whole factor from the top and bottom
scenes.breaks: On a scale you subtract weight, but cancelling divides, so a factor cancels to 1, not 0.
scenes.say: Imagine a balance scale. Taking the same whole block off both sides keeps it balanced. But you can only take off whole blocks. Cancelling is the same: you can only cancel a whole factor that multiplies the entire top and the entire bottom.

scenes.heading: Factors, not terms

right.title: Can't cancel
points: Not through a plus or minus

scenes.say: Here is the key rule. You can cancel factors, things that multiply the whole top and bottom. You can never cancel terms that are added or subtracted. So x plus six, over six, is not x plus one.

scenes.heading: The method
scenes.say: The method is always the same. Factorise the top fully. Factorise the bottom fully. Cancel any factor they share, and write what is left.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Simplify (x² + 5x + 6)/(x² − 4).
scenes.say: Simplify x squared plus five x plus six, over x squared minus four. The top factorises to x plus two, times x plus three. The bottom is a difference of two squares: x plus two, times x minus two. Cancel the x plus two. The answer is x plus three over x minus two.
scenes.caption: Simplify (x² + 5x + 6)/(x² − 4). The top is (x + 2)(x + 3). The bottom is (x + 2)(x − 2). Cancel (x + 2): the answer is (x + 3)/(x − 2).

scenes.heading: Watch out for
scenes.say: Three more things. Opposite brackets, like x minus three and three minus x, cancel to negative one. A fraction is undefined when its bottom is zero. And to divide, keep the first fraction, change to multiply, and flip the second.
scenes.caption: Three more things. Opposite brackets, like (x − 3) and (3 − x), cancel to −1. A fraction is undefined when its bottom is zero. And to divide: keep, change, flip.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Factorise first, cancel second. Only cancel factors, never terms joined by plus or minus. Something divided by itself is one. Now try the practice questions!
